stories.title: Houthi strikes and Hormuz transit friction
stories.what: The Houthis claim a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest, plus attacks on Saudi military aircraft. Separately S&P data shows six VLCC transits of Hormuz on Oct 25, the most since Oct 17, and one VLCC at Bab al-Mandab on each of Oct 24 and 25.
stories.why_it_matters: Ras Tanura is a loading point for crude and LPG routes including the Baltic VLGC run to Chiba; attacks near loadports and chokepoints affect war-risk cost, routing and transit volumes.
stories.latest: Houthis said Tuesday they hit Ras Tanura with a ballistic missile; Hormuz VLCC transits climbed while Bab al-Mandab was steady for a second day.
sources: Houthi Missile Strikes Saudi Oil Refinery
VLCC transits climb at Hormuz; steady at Bab al-Mandab for second day

stories.title: Iran threatens legal action over Hormuz transit rules
stories.what: Iran's Hormuz authority, the PGSA, says it will take legal action from 1 November against Sinokor vessels, claiming they have committed the most violations of its Strait of Hormuz transit rules.
stories.why_it_matters: Enforcement action against a named operator at Hormuz raises the compliance and detention risk attached to a chokepoint that carries the AG-to-China VLCC trade.
stories.latest: PGSA set 1 November as the start date for action.
sources: Iran’s Hormuz authority to take 'legal action' against Sinokor fleet

stories.title: QatarEnergy force majeure on Adriatic LNG
stories.what: Edison, a unit of EDF, says it received a new force majeure notification from QatarEnergy affecting LNG cargoes scheduled for delivery at Italy's Adriatic LNG terminal until the end of December.
stories.why_it_matters: Cancelled or delayed Qatari cargoes change LNG carrier employment and voyage patterns into Europe, which is part of what the BLNG2 US Gulf to Continent route reflects.
sources: Edison: QatarEnergy extends force majeure until end of December

stories.title: Possible return of Russian diesel across the Atlantic
stories.what: Shipbroker Xclusiv reports that a recent US-Russia agreement on diesel exports across the Atlantic could create a new trade dynamic for tankers.
stories.why_it_matters: A restored Atlantic diesel flow would reshape clean product tonne-mile demand on routes such as MR Rotterdam-New York and US Gulf-UKC.
sources: Russian Diesel Returns: A New Atlantic Trade Dynamic

stories.title: Russia forecasts Northern Sea Route transit growth
stories.what: Russia expects cargo transits on the Northern Sea Route to more than double in 2026 despite Western sanctions, though volumes remain far below Moscow's original targets.
stories.why_it_matters: Arctic transits shorten some Asia-Europe voyages and shift tonne-mile demand, and they sit awkwardly with sanctions compliance for owners and charterers.
sources: Russia Says Northern Sea Route Transit Cargo to Nearly Double in 2026
